name: Fatimid Caliphate (al-Aziz)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1.4 million km2 for 1000 (low) and 0.63 million for 1100. The world_1000 polygon measures 1.82 million km2 (mid). Taagepera (1997) and Turchin et al. (2006) give 4.1 million km2 for 969, counting Saharan and Hejaz claims (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires, high).

population.note: Seshat codes 13-14 million for 1000 (high) and 3.5-4.5 million for the reduced realm of 1100. HYDE via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population) for 1000: Egypt 5.0M, Syria 1.07M, Lebanon 0.44M, Israel 0.33M, Tunisia 1.0M, Libya 0.5M, about 8.3M before parts of Algeria (2.0M for the whole country), Jordan and the Hejaz; low 9M follows HYDE, mid 11M lies between the two.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Cairo-Fustat, the largest settlement, 120,000 (Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/221), with Alexandria, Damascus, Tinnis and Kairouan.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Battle accounts of the period usually give figures "around the 10,000 mark" for field armies; the Qaysariyya cavalry numbered about 1,000 in 996 (Lev 1987 p. 344); al-Aziz kept 12,000 horses and 36,000 camels (Lev 1987 p. 354), all via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army. Chronicle figures of 100,000-200,000 for Jawhar's 969 army and 300,000 men in Egypt in 993 (Beshir 1978) are called dubious there, and Nasir Khusraw's 215,000 dates from 1047. Total = the Egyptian regiments plus Syrian and Palestinian garrisons, guessed from these anchors.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Bedouin auxiliaries, Zirid Berber forces in Ifriqiya and Syrian town militias.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Fleet crews (~20 galleys at ~150 each), arsenal workers at al-Maqs, engineers and naphtha troops.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. A salaried army of ethnic regiments and slave soldiers, as in the Abbasid snapshot; the general population was not a military reservoir.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Turkish ghilman (in service from 978) and the Qaysariyya; the 12,000 state horses bound the mounted arm.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: armoured Turkish horse archers with lance

training.note: Rubric 0.75: slave soldiers trained from youth

count.note: Educated guess. Kutama Berber horsemen, the mainstay before 969, and paid Bedouin.

Educated guess. Daylamite infantry (from 978) and black African foot (abid), which grew sharply under al-Hakim; in the 11th century infantry formed the bulk of field armies (Brett 2017 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Daylamite spear and shield infantry

count.note: Educated guess. Foot archers among the black African and Masmuda infantry.
Educated guess. Irregular foot and town levies on pay.
Educated guess. Traction trebuchets (mangonels) and siege towers, reported for the Fatimids since the Ifriqiyan period (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army).

War galleys at the end of 996: 18 ships ordered in 993-994 and 16 built in 995-996 at the arsenal, then a fire destroyed the fleet except six empty hulls, and a fleet of 24 was wrecked off Antartus in 996; of 20 planned replacements only about six were completed. Low = the six hulls, high = the fleet before the losses, mid between.

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: naval service was unpopular and crews were drawn partly from Sicily and Tripoli (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_navy)

count.note: Educated guess. Nile and coastal craft.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: Jawhar conquered Egypt in 969 and the caliphate held the Palestinian coast against the Qarmatian attacks of 971-973 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_navy), but command was split between ethnic factions

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: Lev calls it a "multi-ethnic army with a very marked congruence of military specialization and ethnic origin" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army); Kutama, Turks, Daylamites and black African regiments competed for pay and power

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: paid professionals; salaries paid eight times a year in al-Hakim's early years (Beshir 1978 p. 45, same page)

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: composite bows, lances, traction trebuchets, naphtha.

armor.note: Anchor 3-4: mail and lamellar for the Turkish cavalry.

ships.note: Anchor 3: oared galleys built at the al-Maqs arsenal.

fortification.note: Anchor 3-4: walled Cairo (founded 969), fortified Levantine ports.

logistics.note: Anchor 3-4: Nile transport and state camel trains (36,000 camels, Lev 1987 p. 354).

isr.note: Anchor 3-4: frontier scouting and the postal service as an information network.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (via OWID): Egypt 1000 = 956, Egypt 730 = 1,164, Iraq 1000 = 1,307 (2011 int$). Mid 1,000 weights Egypt, the bulk of the population; low is Egypt 1000 less 10%, high Egypt 730.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Army pay dominated the budget; an infantryman earned 500-1,000 dirhams a year and a cavalryman twice that (Cahen 1965 for 10th-century Iraq, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Linen and tiraz textiles of Tinnis and Damietta, glass, sugar, paper.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Nile irrigation agriculture fed Cairo-Fustat and grain shipments to the Hejaz.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Old Roman roads in Syria-Palestine, the Sinai coast road, Nile towpaths and caravan routes in the Maghreb.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Alexandria, Damietta, Tinnis, Ascalon, Acre, Tyre, Tripoli, Mahdia.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Mediterranean and Red Sea trade; Amalfitan traders kept a colony in Cairo (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_navy).

supplyRangeKm.note: Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1) scaled for camel trains, as for the Umayyad and Abbasid snapshots.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Camels, horses, mules, donkeys and oxen, ~0.1 per inhabitant; the state herds alone held 12,000 horses and 36,000 camels (Lev 1987).

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Sinai desert before the Delta, walled cities and local supply; Syria was contested ground with little population support.

notes: Snapshot = 996, the death of al-Aziz and the accession of al-Hakim; Seshat names 996 as a peak year. Army size is the weakest number: no muster survives, battle accounts give ~10,000 per field army and the chronicle totals (100,000-300,000) are rejected by the modern literature summarised on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army. The fleet figure is unusually well documented for the year because of the 996 arsenal fire. Population convention: everything inside the world_1000 polygon (Egypt, southern Syria and Palestine, Libya, Zirid-governed Ifriqiya and the Hejaz); Kalbid Sicily, a vassal, is not counted.
